hero.title: Useful technology, built to remain yours.
hero.lede: Lowcountry Digital Works builds and improves websites, applications, automation, and digital systems with an emphasis on maintainability, named access, clear documentation, and straightforward handoff.

services.title: Practical systems for real business needs.
services.intro: Projects can be as focused as a website refresh or as involved as a custom workflow tool or a vendor transition. The common thread is choosing technology and access in proportion to the problem.

commonNeeds.title: You do not need to arrive with a technical specification.

items.title: “Our website needs to look and work better.”
items.description: Improve the existing experience, rebuild only what is justified, and leave the source and hosting understandable.

items.title: “We keep doing this task by hand.”
items.description: Map the repetitive process and decide whether a small application, script, or automation can remove the friction.

items.title: “Nobody knows who owns this—or who still has access.”
items.description: Inventory domains, DNS, hosting, repositories, cloud accounts, business profiles, and administrators; move critical assets toward business-controlled ownership, remove obsolete access, and document recovery.

items.title: “The tool we have almost works.”
items.description: Troubleshoot what exists, preserve the useful pieces, and make targeted improvements before replacing an entire system.

ownership.title: Your business should own its digital assets.
ownership.lede: Company domains, DNS, website and hosting accounts, repositories, cloud services, business profiles, and other critical systems should be held in business-controlled primary accounts, with named role-based access for the employees and outside providers who manage them.
items: Named or delegated access instead of shared administrator credentials
Least privilege, MFA, and recovery readiness
Obsolete vendor and employee access removed deliberately
Documented transition, handoff, recovery, and rollback
Secure credential-sharing methods when delegated access is not available

steps.title: Assess
steps.description: Understand the real need, current systems, constraints, ownership, and cost before choosing technology.

steps.title: Build
steps.description: Use the simplest maintainable architecture that solves the problem, with accessibility and security treated as normal quality requirements.

steps.title: Handoff
steps.description: Leave clear documentation, named access, recovery information, and a system that can be maintained without artificial lock-in.

expectations.title: Straightforward technical work without unnecessary platform sprawl.
items: Requirements and tradeoffs explained in plain language
Accessibility, security, and maintainability treated as baseline quality
Recurring services proposed only when they have a clear purpose

local.title: Local perspective, not a geographic limit.
local.lede: Lowcountry Digital Works is being established in South Carolina's Lowcountry and can support practical digital work beyond the local area.

contact.title: Have a system that needs to work better?
contact.lede: Email Eddie with the problem you are trying to solve. A simple description of what is happening now and what you would like to improve is enough to start.
